esercizi.nome: Shoulder Circumduction with Hands on Shoulders
esercizi.description: This active mobility exercise is intended to improve controlled circumduction of the shoulder complex.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright or stand. Place your right hand on your right shoulder and your left hand on your left shoulder. Slowly draw small circles with your elbows, moving them forward, upward, backward, and down. Make 5 circles forward and then 5 circles backward.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.
esercizi.imageAlt: Shoulder Circumduction with Hands on Shoulders

esercizi.description: This active mobility exercise is intended to improve controlled flexion and scapular protraction of the shoulder complex.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand facing a wall with the forearms resting on it. Keep the shoulder blades gently active, slide the arms upward slowly, then return with control.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This active mobility exercise is intended to improve controlled circumduction of the shoulder complex.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand tall with the arms relaxed. Draw slow circles with the shoulders, first forward and then backward, using a comfortable range.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.nome: Standing Wall Slide for Active-Assisted Shoulder Flexion
esercizi.description: This active-assisted mobility exercise develops controlled shoulder flexion while the wall supports the weight of the upper limbs.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand facing a wall with both hands resting on it at shoulder width. Keeping the trunk upright, slide the hands upward until the available comfortable flexion range is reached, then return slowly to the starting position.
esercizi.whatToDo: Keep the ribs controlled, allow the scapulae to rotate upward naturally, and use light hand contact with the wall throughout the movement.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not arch the lower back, elevate the shoulders excessively, or force the arms beyond a comfortable range.
esercizi.imageAlt: Standing Wall Slide for Active-Assisted Shoulder Flexion

esercizi.nome: Resisted Shoulder Horizontal Abduction with Band
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the shoulder complex during horizontal abduction and scapular retraction.
esercizi.howToDo: Hold a light band with both hands in front of the chest. Open the arms outward until the chest widens, then return slowly.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.
esercizi.imageAlt: Resisted Shoulder Horizontal Abduction with Band

esercizi.description: This active mobility exercise is intended to improve controlled flexion and extension of the shoulder complex.
esercizi.howToDo: Hold a stick with a wide grip in front of the body. Lift it overhead and, if comfortable, continue behind the body before returning along the same path.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This active mobility exercise is intended to improve controlled abduction and external rotation of the shoulder complex.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand with the back supported against a wall and the elbows flexed to 90 degrees. Slide the arms upward and downward while maintaining comfortable contact between the upper limbs and the wall.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the shoulder complex during scapular elevation.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand tall with the arms relaxed by your sides. Begin with the shoulders low and the chest comfortably open. Slowly lift both shoulders toward the ears, pause briefly, then lower them with control.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the shoulder complex during flexion, scapular elevation, and scapular upward rotation.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand upright with one arm extended overhead. Keeping the elbow straight and the ribs controlled, elevate and upwardly rotate the scapula to increase the reach. Return slowly.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.nome: Wall Ball Shoulder Circumduction at the Elbow
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve motor control and stability of the shoulder complex during circumduction.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand facing a wall and place a soft ball between the wall and one elbow. Apply gentle pressure to hold the ball in place, then guide the elbow through small clockwise circles and small counterclockwise circles.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.
esercizi.imageAlt: Wall Ball Shoulder Circumduction at the Elbow

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve motor control and stability of the shoulder complex during flexion, extension, horizontal abduction, and horizontal adduction.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand facing a wall with a soft ball held between the wall and one elbow. Maintain light pressure and move the elbow up, right, down, and left to draw a small square. Reverse the direction after completing several controlled repetitions.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.nome: Shoulder Circumduction Sequence with Flexed Elbows
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the shoulder complex during extension, abduction, external rotation, and flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand upright and place each hand on the ipsilateral shoulder. Move the elbows downward and posteriorly, then laterally into shoulder abduction and external rotation, and finally upward into flexion. Return through the same sequence.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.
esercizi.imageAlt: Shoulder Circumduction Sequence with Flexed Elbows

esercizi.nome: Shoulder Circumduction in Abduction and External Rotation
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the shoulder complex during circumduction, external rotation, and scapular retraction.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand tall with each hand touching the shoulder on the same side. Open the elbows to the sides and hold them near shoulder height. Keeping the chest open and the shoulder blades gently drawn together, draw small circles with the elbows in both directions.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.
esercizi.imageAlt: Shoulder Circumduction in Abduction and External Rotation

esercizi.description: This active mobility exercise is intended to improve controlled circumduction of the shoulder complex.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand tall with both arms extended overhead. Begin circling one arm forward and downward while the other circles backward and downward. Continue the alternating pattern slowly, then reverse directions.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve motor control and stability of the shoulder complex during circumduction.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand tall with both arms open to the sides at shoulder height. Begin with small circles and gradually increase their diameter until each arm completes a comfortable full circle. Then reduce the diameter step by step until the arms are again held out to the sides. Repeat in the opposite direction.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.nome: Seated Overhead Dowel Lowering Behind the Head
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the shoulder complex during flexion, abduction, and external rotation.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit away from the backrest with the spine tall. Hold a stick or towel with a comfortable wide grip and raise it above the head. Bend the elbows to lower it gently behind the head, then extend the elbows to return it overhead.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.
esercizi.imageAlt: Seated Overhead Dowel Lowering Behind the Head

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the shoulder complex during flexion, abduction, external rotation, and scapular upward rotation.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand with the back against a wall. Place the arms in a goalpost shape with the upper arms out to the sides and the elbows bent to 90 degrees. Keeping the backs of the hands close to the wall, slide and extend the arms upward, then return to the goalpost position.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This active mobility exercise is intended to improve controlled circumduction of the shoulder complex.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand beside a stable bench or chair in a staggered stance. Hinge forward from the hips with a neutral back and support the body with the opposite hand. Let the working arm hang freely toward the floor, then create small clockwise and counterclockwise circles by gently shifting the body.
esercizi.whatToDo: Keep the involved upper limb relaxed and use a small, gravity-assisted movement generated by a gentle body-weight shift.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not actively lift the arm or create large, rapid circles from the shoulder.

esercizi.nome: Shoulder Abduction and External Rotation with Hands Behind Head
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the shoulder complex during abduction and external rotation.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright on a chair or stand. Lift your arms out to the sides and bend your elbows, bringing the palms of your hands to gently touch the back of your head, the nape of your neck. From this position, push your elbows backward through the available comfortable range, feeling your chest open. Hold this position for 5 seconds, then relax your arms by your sides.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.
esercizi.imageAlt: Shoulder Abduction and External Rotation with Hands Behind Head

esercizi.description: This exercise uses a submaximal isometric contraction to develop neuromuscular control of the shoulder complex, with emphasis on horizontal adduction.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright with the palms together in front of the sternum and the elbows level with the hands. Press the palms together using steady submaximal force. Hold for 5 seconds, then relax.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral joint alignment, apply a steady submaximal contraction, and continue breathing throughout the hold.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, apply maximal force, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the shoulder complex during flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright or stand with both arms alongside the trunk and the palms facing medially. Flex both shoulders to elevate the arms anteriorly to approximately eye level. Hold for 3 seconds, then lower slowly. A light object may be added only when appropriate for the selected difficulty.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the shoulder complex during flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand facing a wall with the fingertips positioned at chest height. Advance the fingers upward in small alternating steps to elevate the arm through the available comfortable range. Hold briefly, then return using the same controlled sequence.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the shoulder complex during scapular protraction.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright with both arms extended forward at shoulder height and the palms facing each other. Keeping the elbows straight, protract the scapulae so the hands move slightly farther forward. Hold for 3 seconds, then return to neutral.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve motor control and stability of the shoulder complex during flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Assume a quadruped position on a padded surface. Keep your hands under your shoulders and your knees under your hips. Slowly lift your right arm forward, keeping it straight, until it reaches the height of your shoulder. Hold for 2 seconds, then place the hand back down. Repeat 5 times, then switch arms.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve motor control and stability of the shoulder complex during horizontal adduction.
esercizi.howToDo: Place the hands on the floor or on an elevated surface. Keep the body long, bend the elbows to lower the chest, then push back to the starting position.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This dynamic mobility exercise develops small-range glenohumeral horizontal abduction with the upper limbs held at shoulder height.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand upright with both shoulders abducted to approximately 90 degrees and the elbows comfortably extended. Move both upper arms a short distance posteriorly, then return them to the frontal plane in a slow, repeated pulse.
esercizi.whatToDo: Initiate the movement at the shoulder joints, keep the trunk stationary, and use a small symmetrical range.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not thrust the chest forward, extend the lumbar spine, shrug the shoulders, or use rapid momentum.

esercizi.description: This mobility exercise provides a controlled stretch to the shoulder complex, with emphasis on horizontal abduction and external rotation.
esercizi.howToDo: Place the forearm or hand on a doorway at shoulder height. Step one foot forward and gently rotate the body away until the chest stretches.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain stable alignment and progress gradually to a mild, tolerable stretch while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not bounce, force end range, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.nome: Standing Biceps and Anterior Shoulder Stretch
esercizi.description: This mobility exercise provides a controlled stretch to the shoulder complex, with emphasis on extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand tall and reach one arm slightly behind the body with the elbow straight. Turn the palm gently away or place the hand on a support behind you.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain stable alignment and progress gradually to a mild, tolerable stretch while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not bounce, force end range, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.
esercizi.imageAlt: Standing Biceps and Anterior Shoulder Stretch

esercizi.description: This mobility exercise provides a controlled stretch to the shoulder complex, with emphasis on extension and external rotation.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand beside a wall and place one hand or forearm behind you on it. Slowly turn the body away until the chest and front of the arm stretch.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain stable alignment and progress gradually to a mild, tolerable stretch while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not bounce, force end range, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This mobility exercise provides a controlled stretch to the shoulder complex, with emphasis on extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit on the floor with the hands behind you and fingers pointing away or outward. Slowly move the hips forward until the front of the arms stretches.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain stable alignment and progress gradually to a mild, tolerable stretch while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not bounce, force end range, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.nome: Standing Scapular Protraction with Extended Arm
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the shoulder complex during scapular protraction and horizontal adduction.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand upright and extend one arm forward at shoulder height. Keeping the elbow straight and the trunk stationary, protract the scapula so the hand advances slightly. Return to the neutral scapular position.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.
esercizi.imageAlt: Standing Scapular Protraction with Extended Arm

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the shoulder complex during horizontal adduction, horizontal abduction, and scapular retraction.
esercizi.howToDo: Lie supine with the knees bent. Open the upper arms to the sides and bend the elbows to form a goalpost. Keeping the elbows bent, bring the inner forearms toward each other in front of the chest, then reopen with control.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the shoulder complex during horizontal adduction and horizontal abduction.
esercizi.howToDo: Lie supine with the knees bent and open both straight arms to the sides. Sweep the arms upward until the palms meet or nearly meet above the chest, pointing toward the ceiling, then lower them back to the sides.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the shoulder complex during abduction.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright or stand with the arms alongside the trunk and the palms facing medially. Elevate both arms laterally to shoulder height, pause for 3 seconds, then lower them slowly.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise uses a submaximal isometric contraction to develop neuromuscular control of the shoulder complex, with emphasis on abduction.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand side-on to a wall with the elbow flexed to 90 degrees. Place the lateral aspect of the elbow against the wall and apply gentle outward pressure without allowing joint movement. Hold for 5 seconds, then repeat on the opposite side.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral joint alignment, apply a steady submaximal contraction, and continue breathing throughout the hold.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, apply maximal force, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the shoulder complex during abduction and adduction.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright in front of a table. Place the palms of your hands on the table in front of you, with your elbows slightly bent. Without lifting your hands from the surface, slide both hands outward at the same time, opening them as far as possible. Then, still sliding, bring them back to the centre. Repeat this movement 5 times.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the shoulder complex during abduction.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand sideways next to a wall, with your right side facing the wall. Place the fingertips of your right hand on the wall at shoulder height. Using your fingers, make them "walk" up the wall, moving your arm out to the side as far as you can comfortably reach. Stay there for 5 seconds, then slowly come back down and repeat with your left side facing the wall.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve motor control and stability of the shoulder complex during extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Support the hands on a stable surface beside or behind the body. Bend the elbows slightly to lower a short distance, then press back up.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise uses a submaximal isometric contraction to develop neuromuscular control of the shoulder complex, with emphasis on extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Support the hands on a stable surface and lower only a small amount into a dip position. Hold the position while breathing, then return with control.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral joint alignment, apply a steady submaximal contraction, and continue breathing throughout the hold.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, apply maximal force, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This active mobility exercise develops controlled shoulder horizontal adduction without assistance from the opposite upper limb.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand upright and elevate one arm forward to shoulder height with the elbow extended or slightly flexed. Move the arm across the chest under muscular control, then return to the starting position without assistance from the opposite arm.
esercizi.whatToDo: Keep the trunk facing forward and perform the outward and return phases through the available comfortable range at the same controlled speed.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not rotate the trunk, pull the arm with the opposite hand, shrug the shoulder, or use momentum.

esercizi.description: This exercise uses a submaximal isometric contraction to develop neuromuscular control of the shoulder complex, with emphasis on circumduction and abduction.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand tall and open both straight arms to the sides at 90 degrees. Draw small forward circles for several repetitions, then draw the same number of backward circles.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral joint alignment, apply a steady submaximal contraction, and continue breathing throughout the hold.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, apply maximal force, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.nome: Standing Shoulder Abduction and Adduction Pulses
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve motor control and stability of the shoulder complex during abduction and adduction.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand tall with both arms open to the sides. Move the arms gently up and down like wings, keeping the movement in the lateral plane and using only a small range.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.
esercizi.imageAlt: Standing Shoulder Abduction and Adduction Pulses

esercizi.nome: Seated Shoulder Extension with Flexed Elbows
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the shoulder complex during extension and scapular retraction.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright away from the backrest with the elbows flexed and elevated to chest height. Move both elbows posteriorly through a small controlled range. Hold for 5 seconds, then return to the starting position.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.
esercizi.imageAlt: Seated Shoulder Extension with Flexed Elbows

esercizi.description: This exercise uses a submaximal isometric contraction to develop neuromuscular control of the shoulder complex, with emphasis on extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright with the back supported and both elbows flexed to 90 degrees beside the trunk. Press the elbows posteriorly into the backrest using steady submaximal force. Hold for 5 seconds, then relax.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral joint alignment, apply a steady submaximal contraction, and continue breathing throughout the hold.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, apply maximal force, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.nome: Shoulder Extension and Internal Rotation Behind the Back
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the shoulder complex during extension and internal rotation.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright or stand. Move both upper limbs behind the trunk at waist level and hold one wrist with the opposite hand when available. Alternatively, place the dorsal surfaces of the hands against the lumbar region. Gently extend and internally rotate the shoulders, then hold for 5 seconds.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.
esercizi.imageAlt: Shoulder Extension and Internal Rotation Behind the Back

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the shoulder complex during horizontal abduction and extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright with both arms extended forward at shoulder height and the palms facing each other. Move the arms horizontally outward and slightly posteriorly through the available comfortable range. Hold for 3 seconds, then return.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This bilateral active exercise develops symmetrical shoulder external-rotation control with both elbows maintained beside the trunk.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright on a chair. Bend both elbows to 90 degrees and keep them close to your sides. Keep your palms facing upward. Slowly move your hands outward, opening your forearms to the sides while keeping your elbows attached to your body. Hold for 2 seconds, then return to the starting position. Repeat 5 times.
esercizi.whatToDo: Move both forearms symmetrically, keep the elbows lightly in contact with the trunk, and maintain neutral wrist alignment.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not separate the elbows from the trunk, retract the shoulders forcefully, rotate the torso, or force the available range.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the shoulder complex during scapular depression and scapular retraction.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright with the arms relaxed alongside the trunk. Gently depress and retract the scapulae without moving the head or extending the lumbar spine. Hold for 5 seconds, then relax.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.nome: Isometric Shoulder Horizontal Abduction with Towel
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the shoulder complex during horizontal abduction and scapular retraction.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright or stand and hold a towel between both hands at chest height with the elbows slightly flexed. Apply outward tension to the towel without changing the arm position. Hold for 5 seconds, then relax.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.
esercizi.imageAlt: Isometric Shoulder Horizontal Abduction with Towel

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the shoulder complex during external rotation.
esercizi.howToDo: Lie on one side with the top elbow bent to 90 degrees and held close to the body. Rotate the hand toward the ceiling, then lower slowly.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This active mobility exercise is intended to improve controlled flexion of the shoulder complex.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand facing a stable support and place both hands on it at approximately shoulder height. Step backward and hinge at the hips until the arms are extended. Move the thorax gently downward through a small range, then return.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This mobility exercise provides a controlled stretch to the shoulder complex, with emphasis on internal rotation.
esercizi.howToDo: Hold a dowel behind the trunk with one hand above and the other below. Use the upper hand to guide the lower arm gradually into shoulder internal rotation. Stop at a mild stretch and hold the position.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain stable alignment and progress gradually to a mild, tolerable stretch while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not bounce, force end range, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This mobility exercise provides a controlled stretch to the shoulder complex, with emphasis on external rotation.
esercizi.howToDo: Keep the elbow close to the side and bent to 90 degrees. Use a stick to gently guide the forearm outward, then hold a mild stretch.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain stable alignment and progress gradually to a mild, tolerable stretch while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not bounce, force end range, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This mobility exercise provides a controlled stretch to the shoulder complex, with emphasis on flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Hold a stable support with the hands and sit the hips back until the sides of the shoulders and back lengthen. Hold with relaxed breathing.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain stable alignment and progress gradually to a mild, tolerable stretch while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not bounce, force end range, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This mobility exercise provides a controlled stretch to the shoulder complex, with emphasis on internal rotation.
esercizi.howToDo: Lie on the side with the shoulder and elbow bent to 90 degrees. Use the opposite hand to gently guide the forearm toward the floor.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain stable alignment and progress gradually to a mild, tolerable stretch while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not bounce, force end range, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This upright self-assisted stretch uses shoulder horizontal adduction to lengthen the posterior shoulder tissues.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand upright and bring one arm across the chest at shoulder height. Place the opposite forearm above the elbow and gently draw the arm closer to the trunk until a mild posterior shoulder stretch is perceived. Hold, then change sides.
esercizi.whatToDo: Keep the tested shoulder below ear level, maintain the trunk facing forward, and use only gentle assistance from the opposite arm.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not rotate the trunk, pull directly on the elbow joint, elevate the shoulder, or force the stretch.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the shoulder complex during internal rotation.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit or stand tall with the elbow bent to 90 degrees. Rotate the forearm inward through a comfortable range, pause briefly, then return.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.nome: Isometric Shoulder External Rotation Against Wall
esercizi.description: This isometric exercise activates the shoulder external rotators without producing visible glenohumeral movement.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand side-on to a wall with the working elbow flexed to 90 degrees and held beside the trunk. Place the back of the hand against the wall and press outward with steady submaximal force without allowing the arm to move. Hold for 5 seconds, relax, and repeat on the opposite side.
esercizi.whatToDo: Keep the elbow fixed beside the trunk, the wrist neutral, and the shoulder relaxed while maintaining normal breathing.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not rotate the trunk, abduct the elbow, extend the wrist, hold the breath, or apply maximal force.
esercizi.imageAlt: Isometric Shoulder External Rotation Against Wall

esercizi.description: This selective-control exercise emphasizes scapulothoracic retraction while minimizing movement at the glenohumeral joints.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand upright with the arms relaxed beside the trunk and the elbows softly flexed. Without moving the upper arms backward, draw both scapulae gently toward the spine, pause briefly, then release them to neutral.
esercizi.whatToDo: Keep the neck relaxed, the ribs aligned over the pelvis, and the upper arms stationary while the scapulae move symmetrically.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not shrug the shoulders, extend the arms behind the trunk, arch the lower back, or squeeze the scapulae forcefully.

esercizi.description: This mobility exercise provides a controlled stretch to the shoulder complex, with emphasis on flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Place one elbow high on a wall with the hand reaching down behind the head or upper back. Move the chest gently closer to the wall.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain stable alignment and progress gradually to a mild, tolerable stretch while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not bounce, force end range, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This sustained stretch combines shoulder flexion and a supported hip hinge to lengthen the latissimus dorsi and adjacent posterolateral trunk tissues.
esercizi.howToDo: Place both hands high on a wall, step backward, and hinge the hips posteriorly while keeping the arms extended. Lower the chest gradually between the arms until a mild stretch is felt along the posterolateral shoulders and trunk. Hold for 20 seconds while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain gentle abdominal control, keep the ribs aligned, and distribute the stretch evenly between both sides.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not force the chest downward, flare the ribs, hyperextend the lumbar spine, or continue if symptoms radiate into an upper limb.

esercizi.description: This supine self-assisted stretch uses the supporting surface to limit scapular protraction and focus horizontal adduction at the glenohumeral joint.
esercizi.howToDo: Lie supine with one shoulder flexed to 90 degrees and the elbow comfortably bent. Keep the scapula in contact with the supporting surface and use the opposite hand above the elbow to guide the arm across the chest until a mild posterior shoulder stretch is perceived.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain the scapula against the surface, keep the shoulder relaxed, and apply gentle assistance through the upper arm.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not lift the scapula from the surface, press directly on the elbow joint, force the arm across the chest, or provoke anterior shoulder pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the shoulder complex during extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand tall with one arm straight alongside the body, the shoulder low, and the chest comfortably open. Move the straight arm backward through a small controlled range, pause, then return beside the body.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This unilateral standing exercise develops active shoulder external-rotation control while the opposite upper limb remains relaxed.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand tall with one elbow bent to 90 degrees and held close to the side. Begin with the forearm pointing forward, then rotate the hand outward and slightly backward while the elbow remains fixed. Return slowly.
esercizi.whatToDo: Keep the working elbow fixed beside the trunk, maintain a neutral wrist, and complete the outward and return phases at the same controlled speed.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not rotate the torso, separate the elbow from the trunk, extend the wrist, or use momentum to increase the range.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve motor control and stability of the shoulder complex during internal rotation.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand with the back against a wall and place the arms in a goalpost position. Keep each elbow in contact with the wall. Rotate the forearms downward so the palms move toward the floor, then return slowly to the upright goalpost position.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve motor control and stability of the shoulder complex during internal rotation.
esercizi.howToDo: Lie supine with the upper arms open to the sides and the elbows bent to 90 degrees. Keep the elbows in the same place and rotate the forearms so the palms move toward the floor near the hips. Return slowly to the starting position.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the shoulder complex during external rotation.
esercizi.howToDo: Lie supine with one elbow close to the side and bent to 90 degrees, so the knuckles point toward the ceiling. Keep the elbow fixed and rotate the forearm outward, bringing the back of the hand toward the floor beside you. Return slowly and repeat on the other side.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.nome: Alternating Elbow Flexion to Opposite Shoulder
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the elbow during flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright on a chair. Keep your arms relaxed by your sides. Slowly lift your right hand and bring it to rest on your left shoulder, bending your elbow in front of your chest. Hold still for 3 seconds, then slowly lower your arm back down. Repeat the same movement with your left hand on your right shoulder.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.
esercizi.imageAlt: Alternating Elbow Flexion to Opposite Shoulder

esercizi.nome: Seated Elbow Flexion from Table Support
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the elbow during flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright at a table with both forearms supported and the palms facing upward. Flex the elbows to lift the hands toward the chest while maintaining forearm contact with the table. Hold for 3 seconds, then lower the hands.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.
esercizi.imageAlt: Seated Elbow Flexion from Table Support

esercizi.nome: Isometric Elbow Flexion with Cushion Resistance
esercizi.description: This exercise uses a submaximal isometric contraction to develop neuromuscular control of the elbow, with emphasis on flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright on the chair. Take a small, soft cushion and hold it in front of your chest, squeezing it between the palms of your hands. Bend your arms forward and press the cushion against your chest, tightening the muscles at the front of your arms. Hold the pressure for 5 seconds, then relax your grip.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral joint alignment, apply a steady submaximal contraction, and continue breathing throughout the hold.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, apply maximal force, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.
esercizi.imageAlt: Isometric Elbow Flexion with Cushion Resistance

esercizi.description: This exercise uses a submaximal isometric contraction to develop neuromuscular control of the elbow, with emphasis on flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright or stand. Flex one elbow to 90 degrees, keep it adjacent to the trunk, and position the forearm in supination. Maintain the position with a submaximal isometric contraction for 5 seconds, then repeat on the opposite side.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral joint alignment, apply a steady submaximal contraction, and continue breathing throughout the hold.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, apply maximal force, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the elbow during flexion and extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand tall with both arms straight by your sides. Bring each hand to the shoulder on the same side, then extend both arms forward at shoulder height. Bend the elbows to return the hands to the shoulders, then lower the arms.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the elbow during flexion and extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand tall with the arms by your sides. Bring each hand to the shoulder on the same side, then extend both arms overhead. Bend the elbows to return the hands to the shoulders, then lower the arms to the sides.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise uses a submaximal isometric contraction to develop neuromuscular control of the elbow, with emphasis on extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright at a table with the palms supported and the elbows flexed close to the trunk. Press both palms downward into the table without lifting the pelvis. Hold for 5 seconds, then relax.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral joint alignment, apply a steady submaximal contraction, and continue breathing throughout the hold.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, apply maximal force, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the elbow during extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright or stand. Begin with one elbow flexed and the hand near the ipsilateral shoulder. Extend the elbow to move the hand forward at shoulder height. Hold for 2 seconds, return slowly, and repeat on the opposite side.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise uses a submaximal isometric contraction to develop neuromuscular control of the shoulder complex, with emphasis on extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand with the back supported against a wall and both arms alongside the trunk. Press the posterior aspect of the arms into the wall using steady submaximal force. Hold for 5 seconds, then relax.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral joint alignment, apply a steady submaximal contraction, and continue breathing throughout the hold.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, apply maximal force, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the elbow during extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright on a chair with a backrest. Hold a light cushion with both hands. Bring your hands above your head, bending your elbows backward, so the cushion lightly touches the back of your neck. From this position, push your arms upward until they are fully extended toward the ceiling. Hold for 2 seconds at the highest point, then slowly bend your elbows again behind your head.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.nome: Supine Elbow Extension in Shoulder Abduction
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve motor control and stability of the elbow during extension and flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Lie supine with the upper arms open to the sides and the elbows bent to 90 degrees in a goalpost shape. Keep the upper arms still and straighten the elbows until the arms form a T, then bend the elbows to return.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.
esercizi.imageAlt: Supine Elbow Extension in Shoulder Abduction

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the forearm and radioulnar joints during pronation and supination.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright with both elbows flexed to 90 degrees and held adjacent to the trunk. Rotate the forearms into pronation until the palms face downward, then into supination until the palms face upward. Alternate slowly for 10 repetitions.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.nome: Isometric Elbow Extension with Manual Resistance
esercizi.description: This exercise uses a submaximal isometric contraction to develop neuromuscular control of the elbow, with emphasis on extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright with one elbow flexed to 90 degrees. Place the opposite palm beneath the elbow. Press the elbow downward while the supporting hand provides equal upward resistance so that no movement occurs. Hold for 5 seconds, then change sides.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral joint alignment, apply a steady submaximal contraction, and continue breathing throughout the hold.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, apply maximal force, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.
esercizi.imageAlt: Isometric Elbow Extension with Manual Resistance

esercizi.nome: Seated Elbow Extension with Hand Opening
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the elbow during extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright with the elbows flexed and the hands closed loosely near the axillary region. Extend both elbows toward the floor. Open the hands at the end of the range, hold for 2 seconds, then return slowly.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.
esercizi.imageAlt: Seated Elbow Extension with Hand Opening

esercizi.nome: Alternating Isometric Elbow Extension into Table
esercizi.description: This exercise uses a submaximal isometric contraction to develop neuromuscular control of the elbow, with emphasis on extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright at a table with both palms supported and the elbows flexed. Press one hand downward while extending that elbow slightly and keeping the opposite arm relaxed. Return to neutral and alternate sides for 5 repetitions.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral joint alignment, apply a steady submaximal contraction, and continue breathing throughout the hold.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, apply maximal force, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.
esercizi.imageAlt: Alternating Isometric Elbow Extension into Table

esercizi.nome: Seated Isometric Elbow Extension into Table
esercizi.description: This exercise uses a submaximal isometric contraction to develop neuromuscular control of the elbow, with emphasis on static stabilization.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright in front of a table. Bend your right elbow and place the outer side of your forearm on the table. Gently press your elbow and forearm downward against the table without moving the arm. Hold the pressure for 5 seconds, then relax. Repeat with the left arm.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral joint alignment, apply a steady submaximal contraction, and continue breathing throughout the hold.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, apply maximal force, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.
esercizi.imageAlt: Seated Isometric Elbow Extension into Table

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the elbow during flexion and extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Keep the arm relaxed by the side. Bend the elbow to bring the hand toward the shoulder, then slowly return to the starting position through a comfortable range.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the elbow during flexion and extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Stand upright with both arms alongside the trunk. Flex the elbows to bring each hand toward the ipsilateral shoulder, then extend the elbows fully toward the floor. Return to the starting position and repeat.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the forearm and radioulnar joints during pronation and supination.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright and hold a rolled towel with both hands in front of the trunk. Rotate one forearm into pronation and the other into supination to tension the towel. Hold for 4 seconds, then reverse the directions.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the hand and fingers during finger flexion and finger extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright with both elbows flexed and the hands positioned in front of the trunk. Extend and abduct all fingers, then flex the fingers to form a relaxed fist. Alternate the two positions slowly for 10 repetitions.
esercizi.whatToDo: Stabilize the proximal segment, isolate the intended movement, and perform each repetition slowly with minimal compensatory motion.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the wrist during flexion and extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit at a table. Rest your right forearm on the table, leaving your hand over the edge, with your palm facing the floor. Lift your hand upward, pointing your fingers toward the ceiling, without lifting your arm from the table. Hold the position for 2 seconds, then let your hand drop downward. Repeat 5 times, then switch arms.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the forearm and radioulnar joints during pronation, supination, and circumduction.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright with both hands closed loosely in front of the chest. Move the forearms and wrists through coordinated alternating circles for 5 seconds, then reverse the direction.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.nome: Forearm Pronation and Supination with Light Resistance
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the forearm and radioulnar joints during pronation and supination.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright on a chair. Hold a light object, such as a small empty bottle, in your right hand. Keep your elbow bent to 90 degrees and close to your side. Slowly turn your palm upward, then slowly turn it downward. Repeat 5 times, then switch hands.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.
esercizi.imageAlt: Forearm Pronation and Supination with Light Resistance

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the forearm and radioulnar joints during pronation and supination.
esercizi.howToDo: Keep the elbow close to the body and the forearm supported. Start with the thumb pointing up, rotate the palm up, return to centre, then rotate the palm down.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.nome: Manually Stabilized Forearm Pronation and Supination
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the forearm and radioulnar joints during pronation and supination.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit or stand with the left elbow bent. Place the right palm lightly against the outside of the left elbow to keep it stable. Turn the left forearm into pronation, bringing the palm down, then into supination as the forearm reaches gently forward. Repeat on the other side.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.
esercizi.imageAlt: Manually Stabilized Forearm Pronation and Supination

esercizi.description: This mobility exercise provides a controlled stretch to the wrist, with emphasis on extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright and extend one arm forward with the elbow straight, the palm facing forward, and the fingers directed upward. Use the opposite hand to apply gentle pressure to the fingers until a mild stretch is felt along the volar wrist. Hold for 5 seconds, then change sides.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain stable alignment and progress gradually to a mild, tolerable stretch while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not bounce, force end range, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This mobility exercise provides a controlled stretch to the wrist, with emphasis on flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright. This time, bring your hands together in front of your chest, placing the back of your right hand against the back of your left hand, with your fingers pointing downward. Gently press your hands against each other for 5 seconds, feeling a stretch around the wrist area.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain stable alignment and progress gradually to a mild, tolerable stretch while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not bounce, force end range, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the wrist during radial deviation and ulnar deviation.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit at a table with one forearm supported and the palm facing downward. Keeping the forearm stationary, move the hand toward the radial side and then toward the ulnar side. Repeat slowly, then change sides.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the wrist during circumduction.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright with both elbows flexed and held beside the trunk. Form relaxed fists and move both wrists through controlled clockwise circumduction for 5 repetitions, then repeat counterclockwise.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This mobility exercise provides a controlled stretch to the wrist, with emphasis on flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Extend one arm forward with the palm facing down. Bend the wrist so the fingers point toward the floor, then gently guide the hand with the other hand until a mild stretch is felt on the top of the forearm. Hold for about 15 seconds.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain stable alignment and progress gradually to a mild, tolerable stretch while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not bounce, force end range, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This mobility exercise provides a controlled stretch to the wrist, with emphasis on extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Extend one arm forward with the palm facing down. Let the hand move toward the floor, then use the other hand to gently guide the wrist into extension until the opposite side of the forearm stretches. Hold for about 15 seconds.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain stable alignment and progress gradually to a mild, tolerable stretch while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not bounce, force end range, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This exercise uses a submaximal isometric contraction to develop neuromuscular control of the wrist, with emphasis on extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit with the forearm supported on a table and the wrist beyond the edge. Make a light fist, bring the hand in line with the forearm, hold for a few seconds, then relax.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral joint alignment, apply a steady submaximal contraction, and continue breathing throughout the hold.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not hold the breath, apply maximal force, or continue if sharp or progressively increasing pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the wrist during extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Support one forearm on a table with the wrist beyond the edge and the palm facing downward. Extend the wrist with assistance from the opposite hand, then remove the assistance and lower the hand slowly. Add only minimal external resistance when the movement is well controlled.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the wrist during flexion and pronation.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit with the forearm supported and the palm facing down, allowing the hand to extend beyond the edge of the table. Bend the wrist so the fingers travel downward, then return to neutral with control.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the wrist during extension and pronation.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit with the forearm supported and the palm facing down, allowing the hand to extend beyond the edge of the table. Lift the back of the hand upward, then return to neutral with control.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the wrist during flexion and supination.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit with the forearm supported and the palm facing up, allowing the hand to extend beyond the edge of the table. Curl the palm toward the forearm, then return slowly to neutral.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the wrist during extension and supination.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit with the forearm supported and the palm facing up, allowing the hand to extend beyond the edge of the table. Lower the back of the hand gently toward the floor, then return to neutral with control.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.nome: Active Radial and Ulnar Deviation with Neutral Forearm
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the wrist during radial deviation and ulnar deviation.
esercizi.howToDo: Hold the forearm in front of you with the thumb pointing upward. Keep the wrist neutral and the fingers straight and together. Move the hand so the little-finger side lowers, then reverse the movement so the thumb side rises.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral alignment and perform each phase slowly through the available comfortable range while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.
esercizi.imageAlt: Active Radial and Ulnar Deviation with Neutral Forearm

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the hand and fingers during opposition.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit comfortably with your hands resting on your thighs. Lift your right hand with your palm open. Bring your thumb to touch the tip of your index finger, then the tip of your middle finger, ring finger, and finally your little finger. Once you reach the little finger, go back in the opposite direction. Repeat 3 times with each hand.
esercizi.whatToDo: Stabilize the proximal segment, isolate the intended movement, and perform each repetition slowly with minimal compensatory motion.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.nome: Tabletop Finger Flexion and Extension Walk
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the hand and fingers during finger flexion and finger extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright at a table. Place the fingertips of one hand on the surface with the palm elevated. Sequentially flex and extend the fingers to advance the hand forward, then reverse the sequence to return. Repeat with the opposite hand.
esercizi.whatToDo: Stabilize the proximal segment, isolate the intended movement, and perform each repetition slowly with minimal compensatory motion.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.
esercizi.imageAlt: Tabletop Finger Flexion and Extension Walk

esercizi.nome: Resisted Finger Abduction with Elastic Band
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the hand and fingers during finger abduction.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright with the feet supported. Bring the fingertips of your right hand together. Place a regular kitchen elastic band around the joined fingers, just below the fingernails. From this position, spread your fingers outward, pushing against the resistance of the elastic band. Hold the open position for 3 seconds, then slowly close your fingers again. Repeat 5 times on each side.
esercizi.whatToDo: Stabilize the proximal segment, isolate the intended movement, and perform each repetition slowly with minimal compensatory motion.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.
esercizi.imageAlt: Resisted Finger Abduction with Elastic Band

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the hand and fingers during finger flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit at a table. Place an old sheet of newspaper or a sheet of kitchen paper flat on the table in front of you. Place your open right hand on top of it. Using only the fingers of that hand, start pulling the paper toward the centre of your palm until you turn the sheet into a tight ball. repeat with your left hand.
esercizi.whatToDo: Stabilize the proximal segment, isolate the intended movement, and perform each repetition slowly with minimal compensatory motion.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the hand and fingers during finger extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit at a table and place your right hand flat on the surface, with your palm and fingers resting down. Keeping the palm still, slowly lift only your index finger, then lower it. Continue with the middle finger, ring finger, and little finger. Repeat 3 times, then switch hands.
esercizi.whatToDo: Stabilize the proximal segment, isolate the intended movement, and perform each repetition slowly with minimal compensatory motion.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.

esercizi.nome: Active Finger Abduction and Adduction on Table
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the hand and fingers during finger abduction and finger adduction.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit at a table and place your right hand flat on the surface. Keeping your palm down, slowly spread your fingers apart as much as possible, then slowly bring them back together. Repeat 5 times, then switch hands.
esercizi.whatToDo: Stabilize the proximal segment, isolate the intended movement, and perform each repetition slowly with minimal compensatory motion.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.
esercizi.imageAlt: Active Finger Abduction and Adduction on Table

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the hand and fingers during opposition and thumb adduction.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit comfortably with your hands resting on your thighs. Open your right hand with the palm facing upward. Slowly slide your thumb across the palm toward the base of the little finger, then return to the open-hand position. Repeat 5 times, then switch hands.
esercizi.whatToDo: Stabilize the proximal segment, isolate the intended movement, and perform each repetition slowly with minimal compensatory motion.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not use momentum, force end range, or continue if the exercise produces sharp or progressively increasing pain.
